The '''TIE/hu "Hunter" Multi-Role Starfighter''', commonly referred to as the '''TIE Hunter''', was a [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] from the [[TIE series/Legends|TIE Series]] used during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Developed by the Empire as a means of countering the Rebel Alliance's [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing starfighter]], the TIE Hunter was used exclusively by [[Storm commando/Legends|storm commandos]].

==Characteristics==
The [[Twin ion engine/Legends|Twin ion engine]] Hunter was an [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] which had a wing configuration roughly the reverse of a [[TIE/IN interceptor/Legends|TIE/IN interceptor]]. Similar to the [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing starfighter]], the TIE Hunter possessed [[S-foils/Legends|S-foils]], which meant that they would open in attack mode and close in normal flight. This was largely because the TIE Hunters were created by the Galactic Empire specifically as a means to counter the T-65 X-wing starfighter. Unlike most other contemporary TIEs of the time, TIE Hunters were equipped with a [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] and [[Deflector shield/Legends|shields]], making them more valuable than most starfighters the Empire utilized. Because of these characteristics, it was also considered to be the fastest TIE variant among the Imperial fleet.<ref name="RS III guide" /> When the S-foils were closed, the craft could not fire its weapons.<ref name="RS III" />

TIE Hunters were [[Pilot/Legends|piloted]] by one individual. They were equipped with two [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannons]], two [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannons]], and a [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedo]] launcher with twelve [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedos]],<ref name="RS III" /> a weapon load-out comparable to that of the [[BTL Y-wing starfighter/Legends|BTL Y-wing starfighter]].

The craft carried a Class 1 hyperdrive, 2 [[Standard day/Legends|days]] worth of supplies, and cost 100,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]],<ref name="Onslaught" /> although in some cases they carried a Class 2 hyperdrive, a [[Standard week/Legends|week's]] worth of supplies, and cost 275,000 credits.<ref name="Stay on Target" />

They also were waterproof, being capable of staying submerged in reservoirs for a week and lifting off no worse for wear.<ref name="Handbook" />

==History==
{{Quote|Using captured Imperial TIE Fighters, launch a sneak attack on the Imperial shipyards of Fondor.|Crix Madine telling Rogue Squadron how they are going to surprise the Empire in the [[Fondor shipyard assault]]|<ref name="RS III" />}}
[[File:TheGauntlet-OaAI.png|thumb|left|180px|A TIE Hunter pursues an A-wing interceptor through the Gauntlet on Arda I.]]
At some point after the [[Fresian campaign]] in [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]] but before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]],<ref name="Handbook" /> the Imperials developed the TIE Hunters, as a means to counter the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance's]] X-wing starfighters.<ref name="RS III guide" /> Development was made even more urgent after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], after the Alliance established itself as an organized threat to the Empire.<ref name="Stay on Target" /> Sienar Fleet Systems did so via data from countless encounters with Alliance starfighters, with the [[Admiralty (Imperial)/Legends|Admiralty]] deciding after the promising results to issue the TIE Hunters to be under the exclusive ownership of the Imperial [[Storm commando/Legends|storm commandos]],<ref name="Stay on Target" /><ref name="CSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> although they had been field-tested by TIE pilots such as then-[[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Soontir Fel/Legends|Soontir Fel]]. During one instance, then-Storm Commando leader Crix Madine and the other Storm Commandos during a mission hid their TIE Hunters in a reservoir to avoid detection, and retrieved them within a week.<ref name="Handbook" /> However, production ultimately took longer than the Imperial Navy brass desired.<ref name="Stay on Target" />

Imperial ace pilot [[Tam Blackstar/Legends|Tam Blackstar]] led [[Dark Blade Squadron]] flying a TIE Hunter, while the rest of the squadron flew TIE Interceptors. Shortly after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], they participated in the [[Battle of the Gauntlet (Galactic Civil War)|attack]] on the [[Arda Base|Rebel base]] on [[Arda I]], engaging the fleeing [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] forces. During the battle, Blackstar pursued a lone [[RZ-1 A-wing interceptor/Legends|RZ-1 A-wing interceptor]] through the narrow canyon known as [[The Gauntlet (Arda I)|the Gauntlet]] and fired a pair of [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedoes]] at the fleeing ship.<ref name="Onslaught" />

A squadron of TIE Hunters was encountered by [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] during his [[mission to Destrillion]], although they were destroyed by the Rebel fighter [[Ace/Legends|ace]]. Several TIE Hunters were captured by the Rebel Alliance, and three of them were used in a successful [[Fondor shipyard assault|raid]] on [[Fondor/Legends|Fondor]] by [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] shortly before the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]]. Rogue Squadron successfully made it past the shields and destroyed the [[Unidentified Executor-class Star Dreadnought|unfinished ''Executor''-class Super Star Destroyer]] being built there.<ref name="RS III" />

==Behind the scenes==
The TIE Hunters appear in the [[2003]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''. Players can fly the TIE Hunter in any completed mission after achieving all gold medals for the missions or by entering a cheat code, and it is stored in a room in the back of the hangar. Its history was further expanded in the 2014 [[Star Wars: Age of Rebellion (roleplaying game)|''Age of Rebellion'']] roleplaying game sourcebook [[Stay on Target (sourcebook)|''Stay on Target'']], as well as in the guidebook ''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''.
